findings.issue_text: [High/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False for real flusher processes because they are created via `self.mp_context.Process` (spawn context, `SpawnProcess`), a sibling class rather than a subclass of `multiprocessing.Process`, so `process.kill()` is never called: a hung flusher isn't killed and `_create_process_for_shards` starts a second process over the same shards, risking duplicate segments to Kafka if the hung process recovers, with the orphan never monitored or reaped (the same broken check in `join()` also means `terminate()` never runs). Fix: use `isinstance(process, self.mp_context.Process)` or `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`, or gate on `self.produce_to_pipe is None`.

[Medium/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:53-62 — `flusher_processes`/`max_processes` is unvalidated: a negative value makes `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(shards)) < 0`, yielding zero flusher processes so nothing is ever flushed while both the backpressure check and memory check are effectively disabled, causing the consumer to silently buffer into Redis without bound. Clamp/validate to `>= 1`.
[Medium/bug] `max_processes or len(...)` silently reinterprets `0` as 'one process per shard', which is undocumented in the CLI help.

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:60-64 — the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because the same test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to `lambda _: None`, so the intended wait never happens and the race it was meant to fix (flusher thread may observe `stopped` in `join()` before flushing after the `current_drift` update, leaving `messages` empty) still exists.

[Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/ — all shown tests inject `produce_to_pipe`, so the flusher only ever runs in threading.Thread mode and none of the rewritten production paths are exercised: spawn-process creation (including pickling of the per-shard `SpansBuffer` args), `_ensure_processes_alive` crash/hang restart, kill/terminate of real processes, or the `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` RuntimeError; the new test only asserts structure (`len(flusher.processes) == 2`, shard counts) rather than that flushing/production works with shards split across processes, which is why the isinstance bug is invisible to CI.

[Low/performance] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:77 — the parent consumer now constructs and keeps one `SpansBuffer` per process group (`self.buffers`) solely for `record_stored_segments()`/`get_memory_info()` in submit, incurring avoidable overhead in the parent process.

goldens.comment: In the SpanFlusher flush loop, metric tags inconsistently use 'shard' (e.g., in spans.buffer.flusher.produce and spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes) and 'shards' (in spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce) for the same shard identifier value. This prevents correct metric aggregation across flush stages — dashboards and alerts filtering by tag 'shard' will miss data tagged as 'shards' and vice versa.
The test_basic function in test_consumer.py uses a monkeypatched time.sleep that returns immediately, but then calls time.sleep(0.1) expecting it to actually wait.

Because flusher processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, they are instances of multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess, which on POSIX is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check will always be false and hung processes won't be killed here.
Sleep in test_consumer.py won’t actually wait because time.sleep was monkeypatched above; consider restoring sleep or using a different sync to ensure the flusher has time to process.

Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:53-62 — `flusher_processes`/`max_processes` is unvalidated: a negative value makes `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(shards)) < 0`, yielding zero flusher processes so nothing is ever flushed while both the backpressure check and memory check are effectively disabled, causing the consumer to silently buffer into Redis without bound. Clamp/validate to `>= 1`.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` does not reject negative values (they’re truthy), so `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(...))` can become negative. That then builds `process_to_shards_map` with `range(self.num_processes)` (empty for negative), and the subsequent loop does `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index].append(shard)`, which will raise (empty dict / negative modulo producing missing keys). There is no validation on the new CLI-provided `flusher_processes`/`max_processes`, so a negative input can break flusher initialization; it should be clamped/validated to >= 1 (or None).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] `max_processes or len(...)` silently reinterprets `0` as 'one process per shard', which is undocumented in the CLI help.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means a CLI-provided value of `0` (possible since `click.Option(..., type=int)` has no bounds) will be treated as falsy and replaced with `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, effectively enabling “one process per shard”. This is silent and contradicts the intended meaning of “maximum number of processes” in the new `--flusher-processes` option help, and can lead to unexpectedly high process counts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/ — all shown tests inject `produce_to_pipe`, so the flusher only ever runs in threading.Thread mode and none of the rewritten production paths are exercised: spawn-process creation (including pickling of the per-shard `SpansBuffer` args), `_ensure_processes_alive` crash/hang restart, kill/terminate of real processes, or the `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` RuntimeError; the new test only asserts structure (`len(flusher.processes) == 2`, shard counts) rather than that flushing/production works with shards split across processes, which is why the isinstance bug is invisible to CI.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows SpanFlusher chooses multiprocessing only when `produce_to_pipe is None` (`_create_process_for_shards`: `make_process = self.mp_context.Process` else `threading.Thread`). All updated/added tests pass `produce_to_pipe=...` (e.g. `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(..., produce_to_pipe=messages.append)` in both `test_basic` and `test_flusher_processes_limit`, and `SpanFlusher(..., produce_to_pipe=append)` in `test_flusher`), so they only exercise the `threading.Thread` path. The new test asserts only structural properties (`len(flusher.processes) == 2`, shard distribution) and does not exercise the real spawn-process creation/pickling, process kill/terminate, restart logic, or `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` behavior introduced by the refactor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:77 — the parent consumer now constructs and keeps one `SpansBuffer` per process group (`self.buffers`) solely for `record_stored_segments()`/`get_memory_info()` in submit, incurring avoidable overhead in the parent process.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the parent SpanFlusher now creates and retains a separate `SpansBuffer` per process index in `_create_process_for_shards` (`shard_buffer = SpansBuffer(shards)`; stored in `self.buffers[process_index]`). In `submit`, the parent iterates `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` and similarly aggregates memory info across these buffers. This is a concrete additional per-submit loop and extra `SpansBuffer` instances in the parent process that weren’t present before (previously there was a single `self.buffer`). Whether it’s “avoidable” is an architectural/perf concern rather than a verifiable correctness defect, but the overhead claim is diff-grounded.
